newsitem.title: UK: FTSE International changes ex-dividend calculation.
newsitem.headline: FTSE International changes ex-dividend calculation.

text.p: The FTSE UK Indices Committee at FTSE International said it had changed the method of calculating ex-dividend adjustments, total returns and dividend yield.
The changes are a result of the abolition of tax credits paid to pension funds and companies that were announced to apply with immediate effect in last Wednesday's budget.
From today, the ex-dividend adjustment going forward will be calculated on a net basis.
Stocks that have already been declared ex-dividend but have not yet paid their dividend will already have been included in the xd adjusted on a gross basis.
But it is now no longer possible to claim a tax credit on any stock that has not paid its dividend before July 2.
To account for this, FTSE International will calculate the effect of including these stocks on a net rather than a gross basis and apply a one off reduction to the xd adjustment on Monday.
Similarly, the calculation of the total return indices will also be changed to a net basis from today.
It is also the current intention of the UK Indices Committee to change the calculation of the dividend yield from a gross to a net basis but to delay making such a change until August 4.
From that date, the net annualised dividend used in the calculation for each stock will not be grossed up by the tax credit and the yield will fall by the value of the existing tax credit.
The Committee said it is not proposing to move to a net yield immediately as there are a number of technical issues which need to be resolved -- such as the Minimum Funding Requirement.
Foreign Income Dividends (FIDs) will continue to be treated as gross and will be included in all calculations at their full value.

The FTSE UK Indices Committee welcomes views on the proposed change to the calculation of the dividend yield together with supporting arguments and all submissions should be made in writing to the Committee by July 23.
